title: What If you Could Explode your 3D Model into Parts?
author: Proper-Flamingo-1783
selftext: The foundation of Rodin Gen-2 BANG (Generate to parts) is rolling out soon!

replies.author: Extreme-Layer-1201
replies.body: It’s an attempt to avoid building something that nobody wants.  Posts like this can be used to gauge interest and determine the direction or readability of a project to save time/money/etc. you’d be surprised how often people spend years and lots of money on a project just to find that nobody is interested

comments.author: fisj
comments.body:
There are \_many\_ AI models and implementations that can generate 3d meshes with segmentation. See below:

[https://github.com/wgsxm/PartCrafter](https://github.com/wgsxm/PartCrafter)

[https://github.com/NVlabs/PartPacker](https://github.com/NVlabs/PartPacker)

[https://omnipart.github.io/](https://omnipart.github.io/)

[https://github.com/3dmindscapper/ComfyUI-PartField](https://github.com/3dmindscapper/ComfyUI-PartField)

[https://github.com/3dmindscapper/ComfyUI-Sam-Mesh](https://github.com/3dmindscapper/ComfyUI-Sam-Mesh)

replies.body: soo cool to see my stuff suggested like that ahah

replies.author: fisj
replies.body: Thank you for your work. This type of functionality builds useful pipelines, especially when comfyUI is involved. Appreciate the MIT license.

replies.author: 3dmindscaper2000
replies.body: Yeah. I stand on the idea that if AI was built by the collective work of alot of people any tools made with it should strive to be free to use. Although when it comes to 3d we would benefit if traditional programs developed some of this tooling into their pipeline.Just because open source can be flaky with upkeep and maintenance

replies.author: Crierlon
replies.body: If you have good retopology, you can easily do it by selecting an edge loop.

replies.author: Hyper3D_RodinAI
replies.body: Thanks for sharing these. What we're trying to do step further is not using the segmentation, but a new method of creating a smooth sequence of exploded states for an input geometry, progressively separating parts while preserving their geometric and semantic coherence. Research paper: [https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21493](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21493)

comments.author: Fluid_Cup8329
comments.body:
Homie discovers modularity.

It's a mistake *not* to create models this way. That's what has kept me away from generated models, apart from nightmare topo. Glad to see it catching up, though.
